 Order

This petition is filed for quashing the charge-sheet in C.C.No.9564/2022 registered by the respondent/Police for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 109 of Indian Penal Code.
2. It is the case of the prosecution that, the respondent No.2 married accused No.1 about 11 years ago as on the date of filing the complaint.

It is further stated that after the marriage, the accused No.1 had taken care of her for about 1-2 years and thereafter, he had addicted to the alcohol and also suspecting the fidelity and used to assault not only physically but also mentally.

It is further stated that hoping for the best, the respondent No.2 waited for longer period, when it went out of control,
she came out of the matrimonial home and started residing with her brother.

Such being the fact, on 27.09.2021 at about 12-30 p.m., the accused No.1 came to her brother's house and started assaulting the respondent No.2, the brother of the respondent No.2 interfered and pacified the matter.
Thereafter, they have decided to lodge the complaint.
Accordingly, complaint came to be lodged against the petitioners and other accused.

3. Heard Sri Pradeepkumar, learned counsel appearing for Sri Bhimashankar, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Sharanabasappa M. Patil, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1/State.
Notice served to respondent No.2, however, remained absent.
4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners that, the allegations made out against the petitioners are omnibus in nature.
Petitioner No.1 is the mother-in-law and petitioner No.2 is the father-in-law of respondent No.2.
They have been falsely implicated in this case.

2 perusal of the entire averments of the complaint and also charge sheet, it cannot be possible in getting them convicted for the offences stated supra.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the averments of the complaint are bald, absurd and vexatious.
As such, the learned counsel for the petitioners sought to allow the petition and quash the proceedings against the petitioners.
5. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the petition stating that there are allegations made out against the petitioners.
The petitioners herein were harassing the respondent No.2 in one or the other pretext and used to scold her by joining the company of accused No.1.
Therefore, the allegations are required to be tried and it cannot be scuttled at the initial stage.

As such, the learned High Court Government Pleader prays to dismiss the petition.
6.

Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the documents available on record, it is needless to say that, the scope and power of quashing the FIR and charge sheet under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is well settled.
The said power is exercised by the Court to prevent abuse of process of law.
However, such power could be exercised when the complaint filed by the complainant or when the said complaint is found to be frivolous or vexatious.

In the present case, on careful perusal of the complaint and also statement of respondent No.2, it appears that the allegations are made out against the accused No.1, who is the husband of respondent No.2.

However, there are no specific allegations made out against the petitioners, in other words, the allegations made in the complaint are patently absurd and inherently improbable so that no prudent person can ever reach a conclusion that there is a sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
Therefore, this is the fit case to exercise the inherent jurisdiction to quash the proceedings against the petitioners.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The criminal petition is allowed.

The charge sheet and its consequent proceedings registered in C.C.No.9564/2022 (arisen from the Crime No.230/2021)
registered by Kalaburagi City Women Police Station, pending on the file of learned I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Kalaburagi for the alleged offences under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 109 Indian Penal Code are quashed.
